policy: query params are sorted by name (stable - the value order of a repeated name is preserved) and re-encoded canonically; tracking params are dropped: any param starting utm_ plus exactly {gclid, fbclid, msclkid} - EXCEPT utm_content, which is KEPT (it routes the A/B feature experience, per the marketing-eng agreement); params with an empty value are dropped entirely (that rule wins even for utm_content); scheme and host are lowercased while the path keeps its case AND its trailing slash exactly as given (case-sensitive origin object storage; /dir/ vs /dir are different resources)
bug_report: Since the ad campaign launched, the edge cache hit-rate has cratered and the CDN bill nearly doubled - origin egress is spiking on pages that should be cached. Separately, two customers report seeing someone else's experiment variant on pages our analytics says belong to the other cohort. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix cache_key so equivalent requests share a cache entry, without breaking existing behaviour.
non_guessable: decision lives in git history (a documented commit), broken by a misleading 'perf' regression commit; git log/blame is the shortcut
decision_subject: fix: cache_key canonicalization - stable param sort, tracking-drop set with the utm_content carve-out, empty-value drop, surgical case rules
decision_rationale: Every cache symptom from the campaign launch traced to cache_key using the raw URL string. The policy: query params are sorted by name - a STABLE sort, so the value order of a repeated name is preserved - and re-encoded canonically. Tracking params are dropped: any param starting utm_ plus exactly gclid, fbclid and msclkid, nothing heuristic beyond that - EXCEPT utm_content, which is KEPT per the marketing-eng agreement because it routes the A/B feature experience; dropping it serves one variant's cached page to the other cohort. Params with an empty value are dropped entirely (that rule wins even for utm_content; the origin ignores them and they only fragment the cache). Normalization is surgical: scheme and host lowercase - DNS is case-insensitive - but the path keeps its case and its trailing slash exactly as given, because the origin is case-sensitive object storage and /dir/ vs /dir are different resources; collapsing either serves the wrong object.
